title: Dedicated capacity: Pool resiliency playbook & staged autoscale rollout (Q1)
creator: Ava Chen
description: Background: As customers adopt Dedicated pools for predictable latency and isolation, we need an explicit resiliency playbook and a staged autoscale rollout to reduce incident blast radius and minimize cold-starts/cost regressions. This ticket captures the Q1 roadmap slice: (1) define pool resiliency runbooks and guardrails, (2) implement staged autoscale activation windows (reservoir + burst activation), (3) pilot telemetry and rollback automation, and (4) run two customer pilots with clear success metrics.
acceptance_criteria: A resilient playbook document published and linked from Console runbooks page
Autoscale staged activation implemented in control plane with gating flags and canary policy
Pilot telemetry dashboard showing latency, p99 tail, token cost delta, and cold-start events for pilot customers
At least two enterprise customers complete a pilot with documented results and go/no-go decision
Rollback automation (model fallback + capacity drain) tested in staging and exercised during one simulated failure
tasks: Write pool resiliency playbook (owner: PM) including runbooks for node loss, zone outage, and pool overcommit
Design staged autoscale policy (reservoir size, activation thresholds, cooldowns) with Eng and Infra
Implement control-plane feature flags and canary rollout path (ENG owners: runtime-team)
Create pilot config and enroll two customers (solutions-eng to coordinate)
Build KPI dashboard and alerts (metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, token cost per 1k, autoscale activations)
Run simulated failover drills and document outcomes
Post-pilot retrospective and decision: promote to gradual rollout or pause
decisions: Adopt reservoir-first approach: reserve a small baseline pool and enable burst activation only when thresholds exceeded
Require autoscale cooldown of 3 minutes by default to avoid oscillation during noisy traffic
Gate initial rollout behind customer opt-in and feature flag; no automatic enable for existing pools
Use model-variant fallback as primary graceful degradation for capacity pressure rather than rejecting requests
